title: scaffold(create-objectstack): measure `npx -y create-objectstack@next` on node 22 / npm 10 with pnpm absent — does 18.0 GA fix the `latest` install crash by itself? (#24445)
body:
Filed by the director seat (summon #43 continuation 5, `session_01QJC7i981TSs9L1CGJK59Ax`) on the maintainer's words of 2026-10-19 in this seat's chat, on #24445: 「等我发布了新的 v18 npx create-objectstack问题就能解决吗？要不要派一个卡测试一下」 then 「你只需要创建卡片」. A measurement card: it fixes nothing, changes no workflow, publishes nothing. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Why

- #24445: the nightly registry canary (`.github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml` job `registry-canary`, `:530`ff) has been red since 10-16 because `npx -y create-objectstack@latest` resolves to 17.7.0, whose generated project crashes at `npm install` on npm 10 (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`). npm 10 is what Node 20 and Node 22 bundle; the scaffolder falls back to npm only when pnpm is absent from PATH (`detect-package-manager.ts`), so the users hit are first-timers on an LTS Node with no pnpm.
- The 18.x line carries two fixes: the blank template's `overrides.vitest` (#23788 / #23805, `.changeset/pre/23788-blank-scaffold-npm10-vitest-override.md`) and `@objectstack/metadata-core` dropping its optional `vitest` peer (#23806). The nightly 「Scaffold with repo dist」 job is green on #24168's head (`a30a6dc4de`, run `39194689420`) — but that job scaffolds with the repo-built scaffolder and framework, not with what the registry serves. Whether a new user gets a working install from the **published** `@next` packages on npm 10 has not been measured; the canary only ever runs `@latest`.
- The maintainer's question is exactly that: once 18.0 is published and `latest` moves, does `npx create-objectstack` work by itself, with no 17.x release?

## What to measure

On a machine or container with **Node 22 (npm 10.9.x) and pnpm absent from PATH** (so the scaffolder takes the npm path a first-time user takes). Mirror the canary's steps at `scaffold-e2e.yml:549`ff; ⛔ do not edit the workflow (Tier H) — run it by hand.

1. **The case:** `npx -y create-objectstack@next canary-app -t blank --skip-skills`. Record the banner version (expected `18.0.0-next.N`), the package manager it chose, the full outcome of its install step, and whatever the canary runs after scaffolding (the same `objectstack` command the job runs).
2. **The control:** the same command with `@latest` (expected: banner 17.7.0, `edgesOut` crash, `objectstack: not found`). If the control passes, the premise of #24445 has changed; say so.
3. **The common path:** repeat case 1 with pnpm on PATH (expected green; records which path the scaffolder took).
4. **Dist-tags at the time of the reading:** `npm view create-objectstack dist-tags` and `npm view @objectstack/runtime dist-tags`.

## Done when

- The four readings are on this card verbatim (commands, versions, exit codes, the install log's last 20 lines on failure), and a one-line summary is posted on #24445 as a pointer.
- **Green on `@next` (npm path):** the reading says so, and that 18.0 GA moving `latest` is expected to turn the canary green on its own; no 17.x release is needed for the new-user path. The maintainer's letter on #24445 follows the reading.
- **Red on `@next`:** the reading names the failing step and the error, and a fix card is filed on the 18.x line (`domain:devx`) before GA; #24445 stays open.
- ⛔ No fix, no workflow change, no release in this card.

## Dedupe

`needs-user-decision` and `pm:queue` cards read in this act: #24445 is the decision card (it names A / B / C and runs no measurement); no other card measures the registry path on `@next`. #23805 / #23806 / #23849 / #23966 are the 18.x fixes and their docs, all landed.

Related: #24445 (the decision; this card's reading precedes its letter), #24168 (the `next` version PR, merged), `scaffold-e2e.yml` (`registry-canary`), ADR none.
